review_mode: source inspection only; no native execution or runtime mutation

findings.issue: Clipped rectangle is mistaken for full bubble visibility.
findings.evidence: boundsInWindow() returns clipping-affected bounds. Checking that this already-clipped rectangle fits root does not prove original bubble is fully contained. A partial LazyColumn row can meet exposureVisible and credit every result span.
findings.minimal_fix: Compare original measured/unclipped extent with visible clipped extent in a consistent window/viewport coordinate space. Retain existing lifecycle/dwell gate.
findings.focused_validation: A half-clipped multiline bubble must flip as allowed but earn no exposure; fully visible bubble earns once after full dwell; scroll away/back resets incomplete dwell.

findings.issue: Cached familiarity/HMAC key outlive vault close while session/store is retained.
findings.evidence: Session close does not nil familiarity; store has no close/invalidate. Cached targetMilliseconds returns prior timing without touching closed vault; observe on same cached day returns true without checking vault. Tests only exercise observe on the next day, which does hit closed DB and fail.
findings.impact: No demonstrated cross-account disk write: stores bind their original account vault and actual ConversationImmersion.observeExposure refuses after engine close. This is a stale-cache/lifecycle contract gap and key retention, not proof of account leakage.
findings.minimal_fix: Invalidate store cache/idKey on session close and clear session reference; retain fail-safe beginner response on closed access.
findings.focused_validation: After close, same-day observe cannot claim success and cached dwell returns baseline; account B never receives account A timing.

findings.issue: Independent chat/bot store caches can show stale familiarity timing.
findings.evidence: Both can open same account vault using separate store instances. Observe reads persisted record within transaction, so same-day counting is protected. targetMilliseconds can indefinitely reuse an older instance cache until that instance observes or is recreated.
findings.impact: Conservative/lagging target dwell, not double-counted exposure or wrong-account contamination.
findings.minimal_fix: Document delayed cross-screen freshness or invalidate on screen re-entry; no new scheduler needed.
findings.focused_validation: Observe on bot store, reopen/read through chat and confirm persisted count; distinguish already-cached timing behavior.

positive_checks: Per-account random HMAC secret is encrypted through existing vault; identifiers no longer allow simple unkeyed dictionary guessing from SQLite IDs. Record kind/count still observable metadata, not claimed hidden.
Account-specific vault paths/AAD and open-account equality checks are present. No concrete wrong-account routing failure established.
Observed records update inside transaction; cache merges only after commit. Duplicate spans deduplicated and same-day calls cannot increase count.
Corrupt/decryption/decoding failures return baseline dwell and false observation; no silent mastery advancement.
Clock rollback yields beginner dwell and refuses backward-day increments; large forward clock changes can freeze progression until catch-up, a conservative limitation rather than meaning approval.
Both clocks cancel/restart on exposure visibility/lifecycle/interaction changes; manually revealed source spans excluded. Familiarity is not passed into knownConceptIDs exclusions.
Target dwell uses minimum familiarity among spans, so unfamiliar words retain beginner cadence. Existing user pace scales durations; exposure remains once/day, not mastery.
limits: Native visibility/cancellation behavior not executed in this review.
Overlapping windows/sheets/other views may occlude a geometrically visible bubble; these checks are not proof of human attention.
Synchronous first-read and committed daily writes use vault IO on UI-facing paths; cached reads avoid repeated rendering IO, but real-device latency is not measured here.
Existing tests cover reopen, same-day cap and language-pair separation, not half-clipped visibility, cache-after-close or distinct-account controls.
root_resolution_after_review: Root reports patched Android exposureVisible to compare clipped bounds dimensions with measured it.size within1px before containment. This directly addresses F1; native partial-visibility validation remains separate. Runtime files were concurrently root-owned; binding hashes are closure-time, not a claim every finding remains in those latest bytes.
release_priority: No additional critical finding identified. F2/F3 are optional low-priority lifecycle/cache observations, not release-blocking account leakage claims.
